sources.citation: Créqui-Montfort, G. de & P. Rivet. 1913. Linguistique bolivienne: les dialectes pano de Bolivie. Le Muséon n.s. 14: 19-78.
sources.note: Reproduces Llosa's Arazaire list (siglum A) inside a comparative Pano vocabulary and gives grammatical notes (gender, plural, pronouns, verb endings); transcription note only cross-refers to their Otuke paper. No remark on accent/stress for Arazaire or any of the languages.

sources.citation: Oliveira, Sanderson Castro Soares de. 2014. Contribuicoes para a reconstrucao do Protopano. Tese de doutorado, Programa de Pos-Graduacao em Linguistica, Universidade de Brasilia. 492 pp.
sources.note: Arazaire appears only in the review of earlier classifications (Shell 1975 used it as footnote data; Rivet 1910; Crequi-Montfort & Rivet 1913 'Grupo Ocidental: Arazaires ou Arasa (rio Marcapata)') and is explicitly excluded from the phonological reconstruction, p.185 (printed p.118): 'Desconsideramos Arazaire (Arasa), Atsawaka, Karipuna, Kulina (Kurino, Kulina), Pakaguara, Pano, Remo, Tutchinawa e Yamiaka, em decorrencia da limitacao de seus respectivos dados, os quais consistem apenas em pequenas listas de palavras.' The thesis discusses acento for the reconstructed languages but never for A…

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan languages and linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History 99. 112 pp.
sources.note: Nothing for Arazaire. Classifies †Arazaire in the Nawa group, Madre de Dios subgroup with †Atsawaka/†Yamiaka (table 1); p.97 states the whole corpus is 'Llosa (1906b) 133-word lexicon', with complete reproductions in Rivet (1910: 227-236) and Créqui-Montfort & Rivet (1913: 46-78). Confirms no phonological description exists.
sources.venue: Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History

sources.citation: Guinness, Geraldine (Mrs Howard Taylor). 1909. Peru: its story, people, and religion. London: Morgan & Scott. p. 229 ('The short vocabulary which follows is compiled from the tribe of Arzaires').
sources.note: no phonology content: a missionary travel book reproducing a handful of Llosa's words without diacritics or comment ('The Arazaires have only two numbers with which to count').

sources.citation: Boletín de la Sociedad Geográfica de Lima, tomo 19 (1906), whole volume (archive.org boletndelasocied1919soci; includes Llosa 1906a 'Las hoyas del Madre de Dios y Madera..', pp. 260-301).
sources.note: Expedition narrative only; footnote points to the appended vocabulary. Nothing on the language's sound system.

sources.citation: Llosa, Enrique S. 1906. Tribu de los Arazaires: algunas voces de su dialecto. Boletín de la Sociedad Geográfica de Lima 19: 302-306.
sources.note: Nothing. 133-word Spanish-Arazaire list with no grammar or phonology. Sole phonetic remark is footnote (1), p.302, on 'Huapê': 'He adoptado este acento, para significar el sonido de la h aspirada' (circumflex = aspirated h). Acute accents appear unexplained on a few forms (Hánah, Marshí, Fuahí, Ca-aíto, Piaíto, Atukiáck, Yaka-akí, Áh, Háyma) -- possibly impressionistic stress marks, but no statement.
sources.venue: Boletín de la Sociedad Geográfica de Lima
